name: discussion
purpose: A threaded comments and forum control: a comment box and replies nested to any depth, @mentions in every composer (Mention Input, people supplied by the host or taken from the discussion), a configurable character count that blocks posting over the limit, delete with an inline confirmation (a deleted comment with replies stays as a placeholder), edit of own comments, and the author, avatar, and a relative timestamp on every comment and reply with the absolute date and time on hover and focus. Visual indentation stops at maxIndent while the nesting stays semantic; threads collapse and expand, replies can load lazily, and top-level comments sort oldest or newest first. The host owns persistence through cancelable events.
whenToUse: Comments on a record (an announcement, a leave request, a document, a ticket).
Forum or Q&A threads where people reply to replies.
Review discussions where people mention each other.
whenNotToUse: A linear conversation or an assistant: use Chat.
An activity history without replies: use Timeline.
A single free-text note: use Textarea or Mention Input.
states: more replies or comments behind Show more
composer invalid (empty or over the character limit)
responsive: Fluid width. Each level indents by the discussion-indent token (half of it below 30rem) and indentation stops at maxIndent, so deep threads keep a readable line length on phones; deeper replies show 'Replying to <name>'. Action rows and the header wrap.
rtl: Logical properties throughout: indentation, the thread guide line, and the tooltip mirror; the reply icon mirrors.
theme: Component tokens discussion-indent, discussion-thread-line, discussion-mention-bg/-fg (in the contrast gate), plus global text, link, and error tokens. Forced-colors mode outlines mention chips and keeps the guide line visible.
timezone: Timestamps are Instants shown in the configured timezone (common config or the timezone option), never the machine's zone. Relative text: 'just now', minutes and hours, 'Yesterday', a weekday within a week, then a date. With a business calendar the absolute date names holidays and non-working days.
security: Comment text is never parsed as HTML: text nodes only, mentions are text chips, and only http(s) and scheme-less URLs (isSafeHref) become links, opened with rel=noopener noreferrer nofollow. Avatar images go through the Avatar URL policy. canEdit and canDelete only hide actions; the server must enforce permissions.
dataHandling: No persistence, network access, or telemetry. The host stores comments: it listens to aui-post, aui-reply, aui-edit, and aui-delete and calls addComment, updateComment, removeComment, or update({ comments }). loadReplies runs only when a thread is expanded and is aborted on collapse and destroy.

budgets.metric: Posting a reply in a 1,000-comment discussion

performance.testedScale: 50,000 comments in the model; the DOM holds the shown page of top-level comments (pageSize, default 20), the first repliesPageSize replies per expanded thread (default 5), and nothing below collapseDepth until expanded.

limitations: Not virtualized: the DOM grows as the user pages in more comments or expands threads.
Replies are always in conversation order (oldest first); sort applies to top-level comments.
One reply, edit, or delete panel is open at a time; an unsent reply is kept as a draft when another panel opens.
unsupported: Rich text, attachments, or reactions in comments.
Enforcing permissions: the server decides who may edit or delete.
antiPatterns: Rendering comment text as HTML next to the discussion.
Relying on canDelete for security without a server check.
Expanding every thread of a very large discussion at once (collapseDepth 50): use the defaults and let readers expand.
